name: skip-link
purpose: The first focusable element of a page: a link that is visually hidden until it receives keyboard focus, then appears at the top-start corner and jumps to the page's main content, so a keyboard or screen-reader user bypasses the repeated header and navigation (WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks). On activation it also moves focus into the target, so the next `Tab` continues from the main content in every browser. It differs from `link` in that it is invisible at rest and owns its placement and focus hand-off.
useWhen: Every page shell (console, marketing site, docs) that renders repeated navigation before the main content: place it as the first child of the shell.
A layout whose `<main>` (or other main landmark) carries the `id` the link targets (`main` by default).
avoidWhen: A link inside content that should always be visible → use `link`.
Jumping between sections of one page (an in-page table of contents) → use `link` with a `#hash` `href`.
A page with no repeated block before its content (a bare sign-in form) gains nothing from one; do not add it there.
related: `link` — the always-visible navigation link; use it for any visible jump.
`console-layout`, `site-layout`, `doc-layout` — the page shells that render the main landmark the skip link targets.
bestPractices: Render one skip link per page, as the first element inside the shell, before the header; do not wrap it in `nav` or move it into the header.
Give the main landmark the `id` the link points at (`id="main"` for the default `href`); a missing target makes the link a no-op.
Keep the label short and name the destination ("Skip to content"); override it with `label` or the default slot only when the target is not the main content.

props.name: label
props.doc: Visible label, the default slot's fallback. Empty uses the locale catalog (`Skip to content`).

props.name: href
props.doc: In-page hash of the element to jump to; the element with that `id` receives focus on activation.

slots.name: default
slots.notes: The link text. Fallback: `label`, then the locale catalog.
